q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Yā, Seen.
v.c: Yâ-Sĩn.

q: By the oath of the wise
v.s: By the wise Qur’ān,
v.c: By the Quran, rich in wisdom!

v.s: Indeed you, [O Muhammad], are from among the messengers,
v.c: You ˹O Prophet˺ are truly one of the messengers

v.s: On a straight path.
v.c: upon the Straight Path.

q: A revelation of the Mighty, the Most Merciful.
v.s: [This is] a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,
v.c: ˹This is˺ a revelation from the Almighty, Most Merciful,

q: (by a Nabi since the demise of Isa ﵊ many centuries earlier)
v.s: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware.
v.c: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and so are heedless.

q: been passed against most of them that they will not have Imaan
(and are destined to die as Kuffaar).
v.s: Already the word [i.e., decree] has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.
v.c: The decree ˹of torment˺ has already been justified against most of them, for they will never believe.

q: around their necks, which reaches to their chins, so that their gazes are fixed upwards
(symbolic of their arrogance in this world which prevented them from looking down and seeing the straight path).
v.s: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft.
v.c: ˹It is as if˺ We have put shackles around their necks up to their chins, so their heads are forced up,

q: We have placed a barrier in front of them and a barrier behind them, and We have enveloped them
(with the darkness of kufr and sin)
(the truth to acquire any spiritual understanding)
v.s: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.
v.c: and have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them and covered them ˹all˺ up, so they fail to see ˹the truth˺.

q: It is the same to them
whether you warn them or you do not warn them.
(because their pride prevents them from accepting the truth).
v.s: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
v.c: It is the same whether you warn them or not—they will never believe.

q: You can warn only him who follows the advice and fears Ar Rahmaan without seeing Him
(because such a person is willing to accept guidance).
Give him the good news of forgiveness and a bountiful provision
v.s: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward.
v.c: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder and are in awe of the Most Compassionate without seeing Him. So give them good news of forgiveness and an honourable reward.

q: revive the dead and record what
(to be rewarded or punished in the Aakhirah)
We have meticulously recorded everything in the clear Book
v.s: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
v.c: It is certainly We Who resurrect the dead, and write what they send forth and what they leave behind. Everything is listed by Us in a perfect Record.

q: Give them the example of the people of the village
v.s: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it -
v.c: Give them an example ˹O Prophet˺ of the residents of a town, when the messengers came to them.

m: but they denied both of them
q: to them, and the people rejected them, after which We reinforced them with a third
“We have certainly been sent as messengers to you people.”
v.s: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."
v.c: We sent them two messengers, but they rejected both. So We reinforced ˹the two˺ with a third, and they declared, “We have indeed been sent to you ˹as messengers˺.”

q: You are mere humans like ourselves
(a Prophet ought to be an angel).
v.s: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies."
v.c: The people replied, “You are only humans like us, and the Most Compassionate has not revealed anything. You are simply lying!”

q: Our Rabb knows that We have been sent as messengers to you people
(and we will therefore continue with our duty).”
v.s: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you,
v.c: The messengers responded, “Our Lord knows that we have truly been sent to you.

v.s: And we are not responsible except for clear notification."
v.c: And our duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.”

q: (only evil can be expected from your presence here).
we will surely stone you and a painful punishment from us will definitely afflict you.”
v.s: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment."
v.c: The people replied, “We definitely see you as a bad omen for us. If you do not desist, we will certainly stone you ˹to death˺ and you will be touched with a painful punishment from us.”

q: (if any evil comes your way, it will be only as a result of you own wrong-doing). (Do you foresee evil only)
Because you have been given advice?
(This is foolish indeed because good advice should rather prompt you to anticipate goodness. However, you say such things because)
You are but a transgressing nation
v.s: They said, "Your omen [i.e., fate] is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."
v.c: The messengers said, “Your bad omen lies within yourselves. Are you saying this because you are reminded ˹of the truth˺? In fact, you are a transgressing people.”

q: came running from the farthest end
of the town saying, “O my people! Follow
v.s: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers.
v.c: Then from the farthest end of the city a man came, rushing. He advised, “O my people! Follow the messengers.

q: “Follow those who do not ask for any payment from you, and who are rightly guided
(who are not selfishly motivated in any way).”
v.s: Follow those who do not ask of you [any] payment, and they are [rightly] guided.
v.c: Follow those who ask no reward of you, and are ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: “Why should I not worship the One Who has created me, and to Whom you all shall return?”
(We have every reason to worship Allaah and would be foolish not to.)
v.s: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned?
v.c: And why should I not worship the One Who has originated me, and to Whom you will be returned.

q: “Why should I take others as Aaliha besides Him? If Ar Rahmaan intends any harm to reach me, their intercession will not help me in the least, nor can they rescue me
(from punishment).” (We therefore have no reason for worshipping them.)
v.s: Should I take other than Him [false] deities [while], if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me?
v.c: How could I take besides Him other gods whose intercession would not be of any benefit to me, nor could they save me if the Most Compassionate intended to harm me?

q: I would then surely be in clear error.”
v.s: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error.
v.c: Indeed, I would then be clearly astray.

q: “I have certainly believed in your Rabb
(and obey the Prophets).” (However, instead of listening to him, the people killed him.)
v.s: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."
v.c: I do believe in your Lord, so listen to me.”

q: “Enter Jannah.” He said, “If only my people had known...”
v.s: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "I wish my people could know
v.c: ˹But they killed him, then˺ he was told ˹by the angels˺, “Enter Paradise!” He said, “If only my people knew

q: “...the reason why my Rabb had forgiven me and made me from among the honoured ones!”
(If they knew this, they would surely have followed my example.)
v.s: Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honoured.”
v.c: of how my Lord has forgiven me, and made me one of the honourable.”

q: send any army against his nation
after him, nor were We going to.
v.s: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so.
v.c: We did not send any soldiers from the heavens against his people after his death, nor did We need to.

q: It was only a single scream
(an extremely loud blast that was needed to punish them,)
(all destroyed like a light that is)
v.s: It was not but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.
v.c: All it took was one ˹mighty˺ blast, and they were extinguished at once.

q: (They are so cruel and foolish that)
They mock every Rasool that comes to them.
v.s: How regretful for the servants. There did not come to them any messenger except that they used to ridicule him.
v.c: Oh pity, such beings! No messenger ever came to them without being mocked.

q: Have they not seen how many were the generations that We destroyed before them
(all of whom behaved as they do)? (These nations were so thoroughly destroyed that)
They will certainly never return to them
v.s: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them will not return?
v.c: Have the deniers not considered how many peoples We destroyed before them who never came back to life again?

q: They will all be present before Us collectively
(when they will have to answer for their behaviour and suffer an even graver punishment).
v.s: And indeed, all of them will yet be brought present before Us.
v.c: Yet they will all be brought before Us.

q: earth is an Aayah for them
(which demonstrates how Allaah brings things back to life after people have lost hope that the vegetation will be revived). (By merely sending rain to the dead earth)
bring forth grains from it, which you eat.
v.s: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat.
v.c: There is a sign for them in the dead earth: We give it life, producing grain from it for them to eat.

m: and We caused to gush forth
q: (In addition to the grains We cause to grow on earth for man,)
We place orchards of date palms and grapes on it
and cause springs to gush forth...
v.s: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom some springs -
v.c: And We have placed in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth in it,

q: ...so that they may eat from its fruit, even though their hands have not made it. Will they not be grateful
(for everything We have given them without any effort on their part)?
v.s: That they may eat of His fruit. And their hands have not produced it, so will they not be grateful?
v.c: so that they may eat from its fruit, which they had no hand in making. Will they not then give thanks?

q: That Allaah is Pure Who created every pair
(male and female of every species of plant)
other things about which they have no knowledge.
v.s: Exalted is He who created all pairs - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.
v.c: Glory be to the One Who created all ˹things in˺ pairs —˹be it˺ what the earth produces, their genders, or what they do not know!

q: We draw the day out of it
v.s: And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it the [light of] day, so they are [left] in darkness.
v.c: There is also a sign for them in the night: We strip from it daylight, then —behold!—they are in darkness.

q: The sun travels towards its destination
(within its orbit without straying from its course).
arrangement of the Mighty, the All Knowing.
v.s: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
v.c: The sun travels for its fixed term. That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing.
v.h: Allah’s Signs 3) the Sun and the Moon

q: (after it passes the waning phase at the end of the month)
like a branch of an old date palm.
v.s: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns [appearing] like the old date stalk.
v.c: As for the moon, We have ordained ˹precise˺ phases for it, until it ends up like an old, curved palm stalk.

q: It is not possible for the sun to catch
(so that the sun appears during the night),
nor is it possible for the night to precede the day. They all
(without entering the orbits of each other).
v.s: It is not allowable [i.e., possible] for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.
v.c: It is not for the sun to catch up with the moon, nor does the night outrun the day. Each is travelling in an orbit of their own.

q: is that We had carried their lineage
(as the flood raged during the time of Nooh ﵊)
v.s: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers in a laden ship.
v.c: Another sign for them is that We carried their ancestors ˹with Noah˺ in the fully loaded Ark,

q: conveyances for them like the ark, which they board
(to transport themselves and their goods to distant lands).
v.s: And We created for them from the likes of it that which they ride.
v.c: and created for them similar things to ride in.

m: (would be) a responder to a cry
q: If We wish, We could drown them
and they will have no helper nor shall they be rescued...
v.s: And if We should will, We could drown them; then no one responding to a cry would there be for them, nor would they be saved
v.c: If We willed, We could drown them: then no one would respond to their cries, nor would they be rescued—

q: because of Our mercy and so that they enjoy themselves
v.s: Except as a mercy from Us and provision for a time.
v.c: except by mercy from Us, allowing them enjoyment for a ˹little˺ while.

q: When they are told, “Fear what is before you
(the punishment and many calamities of this world)
(the punishment of the Aakhirah that is still to come)
so that mercy may be shown to you
v.s: But when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you; perhaps you will receive mercy..."
v.c: ˹Still they turn away˺ when it is said to them, “Beware of what is ahead of you ˹in the Hereafter˺ and what is behind you ˹of destroyed nations˺ so you may be shown mercy.”

q: They turn away from every Aayah
of their Rabb that comes to them.
v.s: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they are from it turning away.
v.c: Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it.

q: Allaah has provided for you,” the Kuffaar
say to the Mu'mineen, “Should we feed someone whom Allaah will feed
if He wills? You are but in manifest deviation.”

(They foolishly fail to realise that Allaah certainly does not need any person's charity to feed the poor just as He does not need it to feed the rich and the rest of creation. By spending on the poor, people are doing themselves a favour because they will be generously rewarded for their charity.)
v.s: And when it is said to them, "Spend from that which God has provided for you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Should we feed one whom, if God had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error."
v.c: And when it is said to them, “Donate from what Allah has provided for you,” the disbelievers say to the believers, “Why should we feed those whom Allah could have fed if He wanted to? You are clearly astray!”

v.s: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
v.c: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”

q: They await only a single scream
to seize them while they are arguing.
(It seems that only after this they will decide to accept Imaan but then it will be too late!)
v.s: They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing.
v.c: They must be awaiting a single Blast, which will seize them while they are ˹entrenched˺ in ˹worldly˺ disputes.

q: (When the punishment seizes them, they will have no chance to do anything.)
Then they will be unable to make any bequest
nor shall they be able to return to their families
v.s: And they will not be able [to give] any instruction, nor to their people can they return.
v.c: Then they will not be able to make a ˹last˺ will, nor can they return to their own people.

v.s: And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.
v.c: The Trumpet will be blown ˹a second time˺, then—behold!— they will rush from the graves to their Lord.

q: They will say, “Alas. Who has raised us from our graves? This is what Ar Rahmaan has promised and the messengers spoke the truth!”
v.s: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."
v.c: They will cry, “Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of rest? This must be what the Most Compassionate warned us of; the messengers told the truth!”

q: only a single scream, after which they will all instantly appear before Us
(to account for their actions in the world).
v.s: It will not be but one blast, and at once they are all brought present before Us.
v.c: It will only take one Blast, then at once they will all be brought before Us.

q: no soul shall be wronged in the least, and you
will be repaid only for what you did
(Men will be punished for only the sins that they committed).
v.s: So today [i.e., the Day of Judgement] no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
v.c: On that Day no soul will be wronged in the least, nor will you be rewarded except for what you used to do.

q: (Unlike others who will be miserable on the Day of Qiyaamah)
The people of Jannah will certainly enjoy themselves in what they will be doing on this day
v.s: Indeed the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in [joyful] occupation -
v.c: Indeed, on that Day the residents of Paradise will be busy enjoying themselves.

q: They, together with their spouses will be resting on couches in the shade(
unlike those in Jahannam where the sweltering sun will be just above the sinners heads).
v.s: They and their spouses - in shade, reclining on adorned couches.
v.c: They and their spouses will be in ˹cool˺ shade, reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches.

q: There they will have fruits and whatever they request.
v.s: For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request [or wish]
v.c: There they will have fruits and whatever they desire.

q: receive a greeting of peace from the Most Merciful Rabb
(indicating that He is pleased with them).
v.s: [And] "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.
v.c: And “Peace!” will be ˹their˺ greeting from the Merciful Lord.

v.s: [Then He will say], "But stand apart today, you criminals.
v.c: ˹Then the disbelievers will be told,˺ “Step away ˹from the believers˺ this Day, O wicked ones!

q: “O children of Aadam! Did I not emphasise to you that you should not worship
(who had encouraged you to worship besides Allaah)?
He is certainly your open enemy
v.s: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, he is to you a clear enemy -
v.c: Did I not command you, O Children of Adam, not to follow Satan, for he is truly your sworn enemy,

q: that you should worship only Me? This
v.s: And that you worship [only] Me? This is a straight path.
v.c: but to worship Me ˹alone˺? This is the Straight Path.

q: has misled a large group from you. Did you not have the intelligence
(that you should not follow him when you had been warned so often)?”
v.s: And he had already led astray from among you much of creation, so did you not use reason?
v.c: Yet he already misled great multitudes of you. Did you not have any sense?

q: (As a result, you shall now be subjected to the punishment of Jahannam.)
“This is the Jahannam about which you were
v.s: This is the Hellfire which you were promised.
v.c: This is the Hell you were warned of.

q: today because you used to commit kufr.”
v.s: [Enter to] burn therein today for what you used to deny."
v.c: Burn in it Today for your disbelief.”

q: On this day We shall seal their mouths. Their hands will speak to Us and their legs will testify to what they earned
(the sins they committed). (In this manner, they will be unable to lie.)
v.s: That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn.
v.c: On this Day We will seal their mouths, their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to commit.

q: If We wished, We could have wiped out their eyes. They will then run to
the path, but how will they see
v.s: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see?
v.c: Had We willed, We could have easily blinded their eyes, so they would struggle to find their way. How then could they see?

q: If We wish, We could transfigure
as they stand and they will be unable to go ahead or backwards(
(then they will be unable to do anything).
v.s: And if We willed, We could have deformed them, [paralyzing them] in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.
v.c: And had We willed, We could have transfigured them on the spot, so they could neither progress forward nor turn back.

q: He whom We advance in age
(that the Being Who causes these changes in people can certainly bring the dead back to life)?
v.s: And he to whom We grant long life We reverse in creation; so will they not understand?
v.c: And whoever We grant a long life, We reverse them in development. Will they not then understand?

q: poetry, nor is it befitting of him
(to recite poetry because his duty is much nobler).
v.s: And We did not give him [i.e., Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)] knowledge of poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a message and a clear Qur’ān
v.c: We have not taught him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. This ˹Book˺ is only a Reminder and a clear Quran
v.h: The Prophet Is Not a Poet

q: ...to warn him who is living, and to establish proof against the Kaafiroon
(to prove that their behaviour and beliefs are incorrect).
v.s: To warn whoever is alive and justify the word [i.e., decree] against the disbelievers.
v.c: to warn whoever is ˹truly˺ alive and fulfil the decree ˹of torment˺ against the disbelievers.

q: Do they not see that, with Our hands, We have created livestock for them and they are its masters
v.s: Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, grazing livestock, and [then] they are their owners?
v.c: Do they not see that We singlehandedly created for them, among other things, cattle which are under their control?

q: some of them as their means of transport
v.s: And We have tamed them for them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.
v.c: And We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to them, so they may ride some and eat others.

v.s: And for them therein are [other] benefits and drinks, so will they not be grateful?
v.c: And they derive from them other benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?

q: They adopt various Aaliha besides Allaah with the hope that they may be assisted
v.s: But they have taken besides God [false] deities that perhaps they would be helped.
v.c: Still they have taken other gods besides Allah, hoping to be helped ˹by them˺.

q: are unable to render any assistance to them, and
they will be a ready army
v.s: They are not able to help them, and they [themselves] are for them soldiers in attendance.
v.c: They cannot help the pagans, even though they serve the idols as dedicated guards.

q: grieve you. Indeed We are Aware of what they keep secret
(reveal and We will punish them for it).
v.s: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
v.c: So do not let their words grieve you ˹O Prophet˺. Indeed, We ˹fully˺ know what they conceal and what they reveal.

q: Has man not seen that We created him from a seed
he is suddenly an open adversary
v.s: Does man not consider that We created him from a [mere] sperm-drop - then at once he is a clear adversary?
v.c: Do people not see that We have created them from a sperm-drop, then— behold!—they openly challenge ˹Us˺?

q: (forgets that he was once a lowly drop of fluid).
He says, “Who will give life to
v.s: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?"
v.c: And they argue with Us— forgetting they were created—saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?”

q: Say, “The One Who gave life to it the first time
will revive it. He has knowledge of all things.”
v.s: Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “They will be revived by the One Who produced them the first time, for He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of every created being.

q: He Who created fire for you from
a green tree from which you
v.s: [It is] He who made for you from the green tree, fire, and then from it you ignite.
v.c: ˹He is the One˺ Who gives you fire from green trees, and —behold!—you kindle ˹fire˺ from them.

q: Does the One Who created the heavens and the earth not have the power to create others like them? Why not?
He is the Prolific Creator, the All Knowing.
v.s: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.
v.c: Can the One Who created the heavens and the earth not ˹easily˺ resurrect these ˹deniers˺?” Yes ˹He can˺! For He is the Master Creator, All-Knowing.

q: His only command is to say, “Be!” and it comes into being.
v.s: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is.
v.c: All it takes, when He wills something ˹to be˺, is simply to say to it: “Be!” And it is!

q: Pure is that Being in Whose hand lies the reins
of everything, and to Whom you will all be returned
v.s: So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
v.c: So glory be to the One in Whose Hands is the authority over all things, and to Whom ˹alone˺ you will ˹all˺ be returned.
